prompt.context: Our client is a large media company in Los Angeles. It currently has two offices: one in Santa Monica and one in Century City. They have made the decision to combine operations into one building and will choose one of their existing buildings, but are unsure which one to choose.
prompt.question: Which office building should the client consolidate into, and why?

clarifying_info.q: Does the client own or lease the buildings?
clarifying_info.a: The client leases both buildings. Both leases have 10 years remaining.

clarifying_info.q: How much space does the client actually need?
clarifying_info.a: The client requires 100,000 sq ft of space.

clarifying_info.q: What is each office currently used for?
clarifying_info.a: Santa Monica houses Video Games operations; Century City houses DVDs operations.

clarifying_info.q: What happens to the unused space in the building they do not vacate?
clarifying_info.a: The client can sub-lease any and all unused space.

clarifying_info.q: What is the size and cost of each building?
clarifying_info.a: Santa Monica: 200,000 sq ft at $40/sq ft/year, build-out cost $1,500K over 10 years, city vacancy rate 10%. Century City: 400,000 sq ft at $40/sq ft/year, build-out cost $500K over 10 years, city vacancy rate 18%.

framework: Phase 1 – Economics: Analyze total costs (rent, build-out) and sub-lease income for each option to determine net annual financial impact
Phase 2 – Softer/Integration Issues: Workforce integration, proximity to clients/customers, proximity to employee homes
Phase 3 – Communication plan: How to inform employees of the move (approaches, pros/cons)
Recommendation: Synthesize economics and qualitative factors into a clear recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: What is the annual net financial impact of occupying only Santa Monica vs. only Century City?
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognize the client is already locked into 10-year leases on both buildings and will therefore always pay rent on both. The key variable is sub-lease income from unused space. Higher vacancy rate in Century City means lower sub-lease rate ($30/sq ft vs $40/sq ft for Santa Monica). Century City also has lower build-out cost per year. Candidate should compare net costs and identify Century City as the financially superior option.

math.setup: Costs are fixed (both leases paid regardless). Sub-lease income varies by which building is occupied. Build-out cost spread over 10 years. Sub-lease rate: Santa Monica $40/sq ft (10% vacancy = tighter market); Century City $30/sq ft (18% vacancy = looser market, lower price).
steps: Santa Monica annual rent = 200,000 sq ft * $40 = $8,000,000
Century City annual rent = 400,000 sq ft * $40 = $16,000,000
Century City is cheaper by $8,150,000 - $7,050,000 = $1,100,000 per year
math.answer: Occupying Century City yields a net annual cost of -$7,050,000 vs. -$8,150,000 for Santa Monica; Century City saves approximately $1.1M per year.

questions.prompt: Besides the economics, what other factors should the client consider before deciding?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate proactively flags that financials alone are insufficient. Key qualitative factors: (1) Workforce integration challenges — merging two distinct divisions (Video Games vs. DVDs) and their cultures; (2) Proximity to clients/customers — which location better serves the client base; (3) Proximity to employee homes — which location minimizes attrition risk from commute changes.

questions.prompt: How should the client communicate the move to employees, and what are the pros and cons of each approach?
questions.guidance: There is no single perfect answer. A strong candidate identifies multiple realistic approaches and articulates trade-offs: (1) Office-wide meeting — broad, consistent messaging but may cause panic; (2) Starting with top/key employees — ensures talent retention first but risks rumors spreading before all-staff announcement; (3) E-mail or memo — scalable and documentable but impersonal, may generate anxiety; (4) One-on-one discussions between managers and employees — personal and supportive but slow and resource-intensive. Candidate should discuss business strategy, talent retention, and office politics implications.

brainstorming.prompt: Besides the economics, what softer issues should the client consider when deciding which office to consolidate into?

categories.name: Workforce Integration
ideas: Merging two distinct business units (Video Games vs. DVDs) may create cultural friction
Potential attrition if employees dislike the new location

categories.name: Proximity to Clients/Customers
ideas: Which location is closer to key business partners or studios
Impact on client-facing teams if location changes

categories.name: Proximity to Employee Homes
ideas: Commute distance for majority of employees from each office
Risk of losing talent if the chosen location significantly extends commutes
HR data (zip codes) can inform this analysis

recommendation: Consolidate into Century City: it saves approximately $1.1M per year ($7.05M vs. $8.15M annual net cost) primarily due to lower build-out costs and higher sub-lease income despite a lower sub-lease rate
Proceed with a structured communication and integration plan to manage workforce transition
risks: Higher vacancy rate in Century City (18%) means sub-lease income is more sensitive to market conditions and may be lower than assumed
Merging Video Games and DVDs operations may create cultural or operational friction
Employees currently working in Santa Monica may face longer commutes, increasing attrition risk
next_steps: Use HR data to map employee zip codes and assess commute impact for both locations
Draft an employee survey asking for location preferences to surface retention risks early
Engage a real estate advisor to validate the $30/sq ft sub-lease assumption for Century City given current market
Design a phased integration roadmap and communication plan starting with key talent retention conversations
